newsitem.title: USA: FAA blocks Rocky Mountain National Park air tours.
newsitem.headline: FAA blocks Rocky Mountain National Park air tours.

text.p: The Clinton administration said on Friday it would block commercial aircraft tours over Rocky Mountain National Park while it devised a plan to reduce noise from air sightseeing tours over the national parks system.

The move came after the Federal Aviation Administration last week issued a rule to limit commercial air tours over the Grand Canyon National Park, which the administration said were marring the wilderness experience.

"Today's action will let us maintain the status quo as we work to develop a long-term solution. In the meantime, we will protect the natural beauty and serenity of Rocky Mountain National Park so that all Americans can enjoy it," Transportation Secretary Federico Pena, who oversees the FAA, said in a statement.
There are no commercial air tours over Rocky Mountain park, but the Transportation Department said several operators have been exploring the possibility.
With this rule, they should not make investments that would be lost if a ban were imposed after tours began, the Transportation Department said.
The FAA in May proposed banning or limiting air tours over Rocky Mountain park. More than 99 percent of those filing comments on the proposal supported a ban, the Transportation Department said.
The rule would not affect general commercial flights that skirt the park on the way to Denver International Airport, only the park sightseeing tours.
